text:
erin_ops: Heads up — seeing intermittent packet drops and RX/TX errors on a subset of GPU instances in eu-west-2 (gpu-pool-A). Started ~03:15 UTC. Impacting east-west model shard syncs.

jay-eng: Can you paste the node IDs? Are these all the same instance family?

erin_ops: Node list: gpu-eu-a-12, gpu-eu-a-34, gpu-eu-a-57. All are the same baremetal SKU (bm.gpu-rtx-48) running 5.15 kernel + i40e NIC. Noticed loss only when pod-to-pod large transfers (RDMA fallback → TCP) happen.

sam-sre: Quick checks: ip -s link show eth0 shows increasing RX errors on those hosts. dmesg has repeated i40e messages.

maya-ml: This matches failures I saw in training sync logs — increased retransmits and timeouts during checkpoint broadcast.

erin_ops: Pasted relevant extracts:

```
# ip -s link show eth0
3: eth0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 9000 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
    RX: bytes  packets  errors  dropped overrun mcast
    123456789  98765    102     0       0       12
    TX: bytes  packets  errors  dropped carrier collsns
    98765432   87654    0       0       0       0
# dmesg | tail -n 8
[i40e 0000:3b:00.0]: eth0: Rx packet had bad crc
[i40e 0000:3b:00.0]: eth0: Rx Ring 1 DMA error
```

jay-eng: Bad CRC + DMA errors => could be driver <-> firmware mismatch. When was firmware last updated?

erin_ops: We rolled NIC fw to 2.2.0 three weeks ago during a maintenance window. Kernel module i40e v2.5. This pattern didn't show up immediately.

ricardo_net: Also check offloads. i40e has known GRO/GSO issues with jumbo frames on some revisions. Try disabling GRO and GSO as a quick mitigation:

```
ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off tso off
```

sam-sre: I applied that on gpu-eu-a-34 a few minutes ago. CPU on the host went up a bit but packet loss dropped to almost zero within 30s.

maya-ml: Confirming — training syncs resumed on that node. CPU spike acceptable for now.

jay-eng: Good temporary mitigation. Longer-term we need root cause: FW/driver mismatch OR MTU/GRO interplay. Can we reproduce with capture?

erin_ops: Started tcpdump on gpu-eu-a-57 (mirror to analysis-host). Saw bursts of fragmented packets/ICMP frag needed. MTU is 9000 everywhere but some switches reported 1500 for transit. That would explain CRC/DMA on reassembled frames.

ricardo_net: Oof — MTU blackhole. Which switch fabric path is used for these nodes? Are they crossing a region BGP hop to other rack with different MTU?

erin_ops: These are east-west within the same AZ but across two leaf switches. Ops for the colocation said an adjacent leaf had a misconfigured VLAN with default MTU after a partial config push last night.

sam-sre: Action items so far:
- Disable GRO/GSO/TSO on affected nodes (done on one, rolling to others now).
- Pin traffic to a single leaf by adjusting routing policy to avoid the misconfigured VLAN (workaround in place).
- Open ticket with colo to fix leaf MTU config and confirm end-to-end 9000.
- Schedule NIC firmware rollback test to 2.1.3 on a non-prod node to reproduce.

erin_ops: Filed incident INC-2026-1782 and scheduled a 30-min window at 06:00 UTC for more intrusive tests (firmware roll-back on a canary).

maya-ml: If the MTU fix is confirmed, can we revert GRO/GSO? Would like lower host CPU for steady-state.

ricardo_net: Yes — once MTU is consistent and we confirm no firmware bug, re-enable offloads and monitor. Also ask colo for packet capture on the leaf during a failing window to validate no corruption on fabric.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: rolling restart of rtsync pods on gpu-pool-A scheduled at 05:40 UTC (user: erin_ops).

jay-eng: Thanks team. Summary: short-term disable offloads + routing workaround. Medium-term: fix leaf MTU and test fw rollback on canary. Post-mortem + RCA after colo confirms config change.

erin_ops: I'll update the incident with timelines and link to captures. leaving this thread open for updates. :thumbsup:
